key_insight: XGBoost predicted pacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM) with an AUROC of 0.831 in patients with atrioventricular block and mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction.
clinical_relevance: The model may help inform individualized pacing strategies, but clinical utility remains unproven.
method: Analyzed 125 pacemaker recipients from the multicenter prospective RISK-PICM registry.
Compared logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost using stratified 4-fold cross-validation and hyperparameter optimization.
Defined PICM as an LVEF reduction of ≥10% resulting in LVEF <50%.
evidence_signal: Over a median 4.8 years, 41 patients developed PICM (32.8%); XGBoost achieved 80.5% sensitivity and 84.5% specificity in internal evaluation.
watch_item: The small cohort and lack of reported external validation limit generalizability; reliance on post-implant measurements also complicates use for initial pacing selection.
paper_title: Machine Learning-based Prediction of Pacing-Induced Cardiomyopathy in Patients with Atrioventricular Block Underlying Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction
